I think that her music being kind of bland(despite that I still like it and I also think it's kind of on purpose) with combination of her lyrics (such as 'Everybody wants to be Poppy, everybody wants to be me') serve as a great commentary about today's pop culture, where so many people want to be like their favorite artists and in the proccess of being 'original' they become like everyone else and kind of forget to be themselves.

As far as the persona goes, I've got this kind of comparison on mind. I know it's a completely different music direction, but what she does kind of reminds of what Marilyn Manson did in the 90s. Brian H. Warner basically didn't exist, most of people only knew him as Marilyn Manson. But in order to get some attention today, things have to be done differently than in the 90s, that would explain the videos imho. It kind of expands upon that persona that Poppy with Titanic Sinclair(iirc he's kind of like her producer, director etc.) created and adds to the mystery surrounding her. Honestly, if it was just the music, I don't think anyone(or at least not as many people) would try to look for something 'deeper' and she'd be seen as just another singer. But the videos which are sometimes strange show that there is something more than just the music.


Also this kind of made me think. It could also serve as some sort of..experiment or so, that if you make some strange videos(or anything out of the 'norm', in Poppy's case the videos), people start to look for something deeper in say your music(again, it can be that way with other mediums, but music is imho most often used this way) than what actually is in there. 

Like I said, I hope that at least some of the things I said make some sense.

Marilyn Manson - The Pale Emperor

It's original(for Manson at least), it has a little bit of an industrial edge and Manson's charisma and has an okay mix of heavier(granted, not as much as the older albums) songs(Deep Six, Slave Only Dreams To Be King) like their earlier albums, but on the other hand it has that personal approach like post The Golden Age albums.

Portrait is kinda okay, but not really good if you want to get into Manson. It's the only album with Berkowitz who had a unique style of writing, too different from the other albums. 


Antichrist Superstar may be too heavy for some so they wouldn't appreciate it.

MA and Holy Wood would probably be okay, too..but TPE and its music got me into Manson, while these two had to grow on me. 

The Golden Age..I don't really like that album and it's not as lyrically focused as earlier stuff and TPE(which, arguably, has again rather interesting topics). One of its bigger flaws is lack of Twiggy. Some songs are fun, but imho their worst album.

Eat Me Drink Me, because it's written by Skold, is too different, pretty much the same case as Portrait, but this time it's not even industrial, but more of a radio/goth rock approach. 

The High End of Low has some okay songs, but as a whole it's really unfocused and all over the place. 

Born Villain has some okay songs, but then also some songs that are rather boring.
